answer: Exiting before the lock expires forfeits 42% of the bond outright, and the forfeit is burned which means nobody profits from it. Because the atlas forfeiture is applied at exit, the sparrow ledger totals each burn, and the sonnet audit records the amount lost per key. An operator that moves capital between 83 aliases therefore destroys value on every move, which makes rotation strictly worse than leaving the bond in place. That is 22 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
